metric.metric: Liquid coolant temperature and flow rate

metric.definition: Supply and return temperature and flow rate of the coolant loop, whether direct-to-chip cold plates or immersion baths.

reading.body:
Liquid coolant temperature and flow rate are operational metrics that determine whether AI hardware survives, not merely how efficiently it runs. At high rack densities, a flow loss or temperature excursion damages equipment in seconds to minutes, far faster than air-cooled facilities degrade under similar stress.

This speed of failure makes coolant loop monitoring fundamentally different from traditional data center climate control. The facility water supply often runs warmer than comfort-cooling systems require, which is part of why liquid cooling improves overall power efficiency. The metric tracks both supply and return temperatures alongside flow rate, whether the coolant path is direct-to-chip cold plates or full immersion baths.

The data does not specify acceptable temperature ranges, flow thresholds, or recovery procedures. It does not compare failure rates between liquid cooling architectures or indicate how often excursions occur in practice. What it does clarify is that the coolant loop is now the machine's life support system, not a secondary optimization.
